Published online:
    September 3, 2026 (dated "2026 09 03", European/global markets day-ahead note)

Geographic focus:
    Global — primary focus on US, with secondary focus on Europe, Japan

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [NO]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
    Bond markets are stabilizing slightly after recent pressure, but the macro backdrop remains challenging. Oil above $90 (US-Iran escalation), persistent inflation fears, and a repricing of Fed hike odds dominate the narrative. Markets have sharply repriced a September Fed hike to ~67% probability. Fed's Williams offered mild pushback, citing need for more data. Key near-term catalysts: Waller speech Thursday, NFP Friday, CPI September 11. BOJ rate hike expectations are building on strong Japan services data, supporting the yen and easing JGB pressure marginally. Broadcom's AI chip outlook was strong but stock reaction was negative. Equity futures marginally positive.

Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US yields, US interest rates?
Relevance: YES (the Fed rate path, bond yields, and US macro data are the clear central theme of the article)

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 85 (dominant near-term narrative — market odds, Waller framing, and oil/inflation backdrop all point hawkish)
Probability of increase: 67% (as cited directly from CME FedWatch for September meeting)

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 25 (Williams' data-dependent caution introduces a hold narrative, but it is secondary)
Probability of holding: 33% (implied residual from the 67% hike probability cited)

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 0 (no mention of cuts; entirely absent from the article's framing)
Probability of decrease: 0%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: +55 (net hawkish — oil above $90 sustaining inflation pressure, market odds sharply repriced higher for a September hike from 37% to 67% in one week; Williams' pushback is mild and data-conditional, not a firm hold signal; Waller — a known hawk — is next up to speak, adding hawkish skew to near-term rate expectations)
